context.guidance: Serialise only the fields a response needs, using explicit allow-lists or response shapes rather than whole models or nested records. Remove Personal Data Elements the requester is not entitled to see, so each response stays within the Purpose for which the data was collected under §6(1). Apply the same field limits on every route that returns the same record, as Rule 6(1)(b) requires for access control.

value.fix: Don't send the whole `updatedUser` model back. Build the response from an explicit allow-list of fields, for example: `const { _id, name, email, avatar, role, updatedAt } = updatedUser; res.json({ id: _id, name, email, avatar, role, updatedAt });`. Better still, put this in a shared serializer such as `toPublicUser(user)` and use it on every route that returns a user record (get profile, update profile, login/register, admin lists), so each route applies the same field limits. Also exclude sensitive fields at the query level, for example `User.findByIdAndUpdate(id, update, { new: true }).select('-password -resetToken -resetTokenExpiry -__v').lean()`, or set `select: false` / a `toJSON` transform on those schema paths. That way password hashes, tokens, internal flags and any personal data the requester isn't entitled to see never go out in the response. Add a test that checks the update response contains only the allowed keys.
